issue.title: Align release summary with blocking acceptance gate outcome

summary: The blocker is not only the parse failure in scripts/check-writing-helper.ps1. The deeper mismatch is that scripts/release_check_summary.py computes GO or NO_GO from its own blocking checks array, while the release strategy, sign-off documentation, and CI gate definition treat writing-helper acceptance as a required blocking gate outside that array. The retained release artifacts inherit the summary script's blind spot, and the current static governance validators do not detect that drift.

relevant_files.summary: Builds the blocking checks array, computes decision from blocking FAIL entries only, writes release-check-summary.md and .workflow/evidence/release/release-readiness-artifact.json, and only mentions the acceptance workflow in narrative output rather than executing or evaluating it.
Human-readable output from the summary script. Current retained snapshot says Decision: GO with no blocking failures.
Machine-readable retained evidence generated by the summary script. Current artifact records decision GO and no go_no_go_reasons, so it mirrors the summary script's modeled blocking set.

Defines the authoritative local sign-off sequence. It requires strict writing-helper acceptance before the consolidated release snapshot and still says release-check-summary.md must end in Decision: GO.

Defines the primary CI release gate. It runs a Linux gate job and a separate reusable Windows writing-helper-acceptance job, so the acceptance gate is part of release blocking semantics even though it is not modeled inside the summary script's checks list.
Reusable/manual Windows acceptance workflow. Starts the gateway, waits for health, and runs ./scripts/check-writing-helper.ps1 in strict mode.
Actual blocking acceptance command. The 2026-04-14 validation session captured parser errors from corrupted text literals before request-level assertions could run.

Static governance gate that enforces anchor presence across workflows, docs, and release summary source. It checks that external-release-gate references writing-helper acceptance and that SIGN_OFF exposes the command, but it does not enforce that release_check_summary.py incorporates the acceptance outcome into final decision logic.

Static authority-alignment checker. Current payload only checks repository anchor consistency across workflow/runtime/docs files and does not inspect SIGN_OFF, release-check-summary.md, release-readiness-artifact.json, or live acceptance execution results.

Current retained alignment artifact reports PASS with 92/92 rules and 14 checked files, which explains why evidence can look formally aligned while still disagreeing with the actual blocking gate outcome.
Validation strategy explicitly includes ./scripts/check-writing-helper.ps1 -Strict -Port 18080 -Host 127.0.0.1 as part of the blocking L3 release proof.
Concludes the session is NO_GO because the strict writing-helper acceptance gate failed even though release_check_summary.py exited 0 and refreshed GO evidence.

Regression tests cover delivery_gate anchors, authority_alignment_signal, and the shared desktop local gate contract between SIGN_OFF and release_check_summary.py. There is no comparable regression asserting that writing-helper acceptance is part of the summary decision contract.
Points L4 release or handoff execution at docs/release/SIGN_OFF.md as the authoritative checklist, so it inherits the stricter gate definition rather than the narrower summary-script model.
Documents that release_check_summary.py covers authority alignment and packaging dry-run, but refers readers to SIGN_OFF for writing-helper acceptance and broader sign-off sequence.

dependencies.reason: These are the commands and signals currently included in the summary script's blocking decision set. Writing-helper acceptance is not in this list.
The external release gate delegates the Windows acceptance gate to a separate reusable workflow job.
SIGN_OFF defines the local sequence, references the reusable CI equivalent, and requires the summary snapshot after the acceptance step.
Current authority alignment is scoped to static repo anchors and does not cover sign-off execution truth.
Current regressions validate static contracts around governance and release summary behavior but not the missing acceptance-gate inclusion.

existing_patterns: The release summary uses a deterministic checks array and computes GO when no blocking entries in that array are FAIL.

Static governance validation is split: delivery_gate.py enforces anchor presence and check_authority_alignment.py enforces static wording or contract alignment, but neither validates live downstream gate outcomes.
Release sign-off semantics are defined more broadly in docs and CI than in the summary script: the Windows writing-helper acceptance gate is modeled as a separate workflow or manual step.
Retained release artifacts are generated from the summary script, so any omission in the script propagates into release-check-summary.md and release-readiness-artifact.json.

key_findings: The current summary decision model omits writing-helper acceptance entirely. A text search of scripts/release_check_summary.py only finds the acceptance workflow in narrative output, not in the executed checks list or go_no_go_reasons logic.

The strategy, sign-off documentation, and CI release gate all treat strict writing-helper acceptance as blocking release proof, so the effective gate set for release sign-off is broader than the summary script's gate set.

The authority-alignment PASS artifact is not enough to prove sign-off correctness because its checked_files list does not cover docs/release/SIGN_OFF.md, release-check-summary.md, or release-readiness-artifact.json, and it does not ingest runtime gate outcomes.

The quality report from TST-release-validation-2026-04-14 is the best operational truth source for this issue: it records the failed acceptance gate, the GO summary mismatch, and the required rerun path.
Current governance tests already encode some release summary contract expectations, so the cleanest remediation path is likely to extend those tests rather than invent a new validation surface.
fix_scope_candidates: scripts/release_check_summary.py decision model and retained artifact generation
Potentially scripts/delivery_gate.py or scripts/check_authority_alignment.py if static validation should also detect summary-versus-signoff drift
Possibly docs/release/SIGN_OFF.md, docs/testing/TEST_TIER_MATRIX.md, and docs/release/RELEASE_NOTES.md if wording needs to be tightened after code changes
questions_for_planner: Should the summary script execute the writing-helper acceptance gate directly, or should it consume explicit evidence from the separate acceptance run and fail when that evidence is missing or failed?
Should authority alignment or delivery gate be expanded to assert that release_check_summary.py includes the writing-helper acceptance contract, so future drift is caught statically?
Should release-check-summary.md be allowed to say GO only when the broader SIGN_OFF blocking set has passed, even if some gates remain external or manual?
